title: CCA Workshop 04 — Prompt Engineering & Structured Output
description: This package contains questions specifically related to the CCA Workshop 04 material.

grounding.text:
Domain 4 - 20%

##### Prompt Engineering & Structured Output

Domain 4 - 20% of the CCA exam

##### IN THIS MODULE:

- F Explicit criteria vs vague instructions
- F Few-shot examples for edge cases
- F tool\_use JSON schemas for guaranteed structure
- F Validation loops and retry-with-feedback
- F Batch API for cost-optimized bulk processing

90 PRACTICE QUESTIONS - 30 BEGINNER · 30 INTERMEDIATE · 30 ADVANCED

##### QUESTION BANK OVERVIEW

| Level        | Questions   | Focus                                                 |
|--------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Beginner     | Q1-Q30      | Core concepts, terminology, and foundational patterns |
| Intermediate | Q31-Q60     | Application scenarios, design decisions, trade-offs   |
| Advanced     | Q61-Q90     | Production architecture, edge cases, system design    |

##### HOW TO USE THIS MODULE

Work through each level in order. For Beginner questions, aim for 90%+ before moving to Intermediate. For Intermediate, 80%+ before Advanced. Each question includes the correct answer and a full explanation - read the explanation even for questions you answered correctly to understand the underlying principle. The exam tests judgment, not memorization.

##### BEGINNER QUESTIONS

Questions 1-30

##### Q1. What distinguishes explicit criteria from vague instructions in prompt engineering?

- A) Explicit criteria are longer; vague instructions are shorter
- B) Explicit criteria define e

questions.stem: What distinguishes explicit criteria from vague instructions in prompt engineering?

options.text: Explicit criteria are longer; vague instructions are shorter
Explicit criteria define exactly what to report, what to skip, and concrete conditions for each eliminating ambiguity. Vague instructions use subjective terms like 'be thorough' or 'be conservative'
Explicit criteria use bullet points; vague instructions use prose
Explicit criteria are for structured output; vague instructions are for conversational use

questions.stem: Why does adding 'only report high-confidence findings' to a review prompt fail to improve precision?

options.text: Claude ignores confidence-based instructions
'High confidence' is a subjective threshold that Claude calibrates differently each call - it doesn't map to a consistent precision level across runs
Confidence-based filtering requires extended thinking mode
Claude reports all findings regardless of confidence - instructions don't affect this

questions.stem: When are few-shot examples most valuable in a prompt?

options.text: When you want Claude to follow instructions more carefully
When detailed instructions alone produce inconsistent output - examples show exactly what you want, including for ambiguous edge cases
Few-shot examples are only for beginners - expert prompts don't need them
When the task requires real-time web data

questions.stem: What makes a few-shot example most useful for a classification task?

options.text: Including as many examples as possible (50+)
Showing 2-4 examples that cover the most ambiguous cases - scenarios where reasonable people might disagree - with the correct classification and why
Including only positive examples of the desired behavior
Using simple, unambiguous examples so Claude learns the pattern easily

questions.stem: What is the fundamental limitation of asking Claude to 'respond in JSON'?

options.text: Claude cannot generate JSON directly
JSON output requested via prompt is probabilistic - Claude may add prose, use markdown fences (```json), or produce invalid syntax, especially on edge cases
JSON responses are significantly slower than text responses
JSON output requires a special API endpoint

questions.stem: In a tool use JSON schema, when should a field be marked as nullable (type: ['string', 'null'])?

options.text: Never - all fields should be required strings
When the source document may not contain that information - nullable prevents Claude from hallucinating values to satisfy a required field
Only for optional metadata fields
When the field contains numbers that might be zero

questions.stem: What is retry-with-error-feedback in extraction quality loops?

options.text: Automatically retrying failed API calls after a network error
When validation fails, appending the specific validation errors to the conversation and requesting correction - giving Claude concrete guidance on what to fix
Retrying with a more capable model after the first model fails
Resubmitting the same request without changes until it succeeds

questions.stem: What types of errors can tool_use JSON schemas prevent?

options.text: All errors - tool use schemas guarantee perfect extraction
Syntax errors (malformed JSON, wrong types) - but NOT semantic errors like values that don't sum correctly or data in wrong fields
Only missing field errors
Only type mismatch errors

questions.stem: What is the Message Batches API's primary advantage?

options.text: Faster responses than the synchronous API
50% cost reduction for latency-tolerant workloads processed within 24 hours
Support for longer context windows than synchronous calls
Automatic retry logic for failed requests

questions.stem: What is a semantic validation error (as opposed to a schema/syntax error)?

options.text: An error in the meaning of the prompt
An error where the JSON structure is valid but values are logically inconsistent - like line items that don't sum to the stated total
An error that occurs when the wrong model is used
A validation error that requires human review

questions.stem: What does the custom_id field in the Batch API enable?

options.text: Grouping related batch requests for parallel processing
Correlating batch request/response pairs - you set it on each request and it appears on the corresponding result for matching
Setting processing priority within a batch
Identifying the model version used for each request

questions.stem: Why is the Batch API inappropriate for a pre-merge code review that blocks PR deployment?

options.text: The Batch API doesn't support code review tasks
The Batch API has no guaranteed latency SLA - results may take up to 24 hours, which would block PRs for an unacceptably long time
Batch processing produces lower quality reviews than synchronous calls
Pre-merge reviews require streaming output which batch doesn't support

questions.stem: What is a self-correction validation flow in structured extraction?

options.text: Claude automatically re-runs extraction until it produces valid output
Extracting both a calculated value and a stated value (e.g., calculated_total and stated_total), flagging discrepancies with a conflict_detected boolean for downstream handling
Asking a second model to validate the first model's extraction
Running the same extraction prompt 3 times and using majority voting

questions.stem: When is retry-with-feedback NOT effective?

options.text: When the extraction has semantic errors
When the required information simply doesn't exist in the source document - retrying with better instructions won't create data that isn't there
When the first extraction was mostly correct
When using claude-haiku instead of claude-sonnet

questions.stem: What does the detected_pattern field in a code review findings schema enable?

options.text: Pattern matching against known security vulnerabilities
Tracking which code patterns trigger findings so you can analyze false positive patterns when developers dismiss findings
Detecting the programming language and framework automatically
Identifying duplicate findings across multiple review runs

questions.stem: What is the 'format normalization rules + strict schema' combination for?

options.text: Compressing JSON output for efficiency
Handling inconsistent source formatting: schema enforces output structure while normalization rules in the prompt handle varied inputs (e.g., date formats, currency symbols)
Converting between different JSON schema versions
Ensuring consistent field ordering in JSON output

questions.stem: Why does a high false positive rate in one review category undermine trust in accurate categories?

options.text: False positives increase review latency, causing developers to skip all reviews
Developers learn to dismiss the review tool globally when they frequently encounter incorrect findings, even in categories where findings are accurate
False positives consume context window space needed for accurate findings
The review model penalizes accuracy when false positive rates are high

questions.stem: What is multi-instance review and why does it outperform self-review?

options.text: Running multiple review passes with the same model instance

Using a completely separate Claude instance (fresh context, no generation history) for review - it hasn't formed opinions about the code and catches issues the generating instance would rationalize away
Reviewing with multiple models (Claude + GPT + Gemini) and taking the consensus
Running the same review prompt multiple times and aggregating results

questions.stem: What does the enum approach with 'other' + detail field accomplish in JSON schemas?

options.text: It limits valid enum values to exactly what's listed
It provides extensible categorization: known values use the enum for reliable classification; novel values use 'other' + a detail string that preserves the specifics without schema violation
It prevents Claude from using values not in the enum list
It's a workaround for the 50-enum limit in JSON schemas

questions.stem: When should you use the Batch API vs. prompt caching for cost optimization?

options.text: They are interchangeable - use whichever is easier to implement

Use Batch API for latency-tolerant bulk processing (50% cost reduction). Use prompt caching for repeated calls with stable large prompts (up to 90% savings on the cached portion). They can be combined.
Batch API is always better - it saves more than caching
Prompt caching is deprecated in favor of the Batch API

questions.stem: What is 'chain-of-thought prompting' and when should you use it?

options.text: A technique that chains multiple API calls together
Asking Claude to reason step-by-step before producing an answer - improves accuracy on multi-step reasoning tasks like math, logic, and complex analysis
Linking prompt templates together for complex workflows
A way to chain tool calls in a specific order

questions.stem: What is the role of negative examples in few-shot prompting?

options.text: Negative examples confuse Claude - use only positive examples
Negative examples show what NOT to report/do, teaching Claude to avoid specific failure modes and improving precision
Negative examples are only useful for classification tasks
Negative examples require a special 'negative' field in the prompt

questions.stem: What makes a code review instruction 'actionable' vs. vague?

options.text: Actionable instructions are longer and more detailed
Actionable: specifies exact categories to check, what constitutes a finding in each category, and required output format. Vague: 'review for quality' or 'check for issues'
Actionable instructions use bullet points; vague use paragraphs
Actionable instructions are written in imperative form

questions.stem: What is the 'temperature' parameter's effect on structured output tasks?

options.text: Temperature has no effect on structured output - use tool_use for that
Lower temperature (0.0-0.3) produces more consistent, reproducible structured outputs; higher temperature introduces more variety but can cause schema deviations on complex structures
Higher temperature produces better structured output by allowing more creativity
Temperature only affects the speed of generation, not the content

questions.stem: What does it mean to 'specify the output audience' in a prompt?

options.text: Specifying which team member will receive the output
Telling Claude who will read and use the output - this shapes vocabulary level, assumed background knowledge, and appropriate detail depth
A legal disclaimer requirement for AI-generated content
Specifying the file format of the output

questions.stem: What is 'output length calibration' in prompt engineering?

options.text: Setting max_tokens to limit response length
Specifying the appropriate response length in the prompt - preventing both verbosity (unnecessary filler) and truncation (missing important details)
Post-processing to trim responses to a target length
A model parameter that controls output verbosity

questions.stem: What is the 'system prompt as persona' technique and what are its benefits?

options.text: Using the system prompt to make Claude pretend to be a different AI
Giving Claude a consistent role/persona (e.g., 'You are a senior security engineer') that shapes its perspective, vocabulary, and response style for all turns in the conversation
A technique for creating chatbot characters for entertainment
Assigning a system prompt ID for tracking purposes

questions.stem: Why should you define 'what not to include' in extraction prompts?

options.text: Negative constraints reduce output length, saving tokens
Without boundaries, Claude may include neighboring context, summaries, interpretations, or formatting that interferes with your parsing logic
Negative constraints are processed faster than positive instructions
This is a defensive prompt technique against adversarial inputs

questions.stem: What is 'conditional instruction' in prompt engineering?

options.text: Instructions that only apply to certain Claude models
If-then instructions that cover branching scenarios: 'If the document has a date, extract it in ISO format. If no date is present, return null. If multiple dates are present, return the most recent.'
Instructions that are activated by specific trigger words in user input
Nested prompts that call sub-prompts based on the first response

questions.stem: What does the 'role-task-output format' prompt structure provide?

options.text: A way to assign multiple roles to Claude in one call

A systematic prompt organization: (1) role sets context/expertise, (2) task describes what to do, (3) output format specifies exactly how results should be structured - producing consistent, appropriately-scoped outputs
A template format required by the Anthropic API
A three-turn conversation pattern for complex tasks

questions.stem: You are building a multi-document extraction pipeline. Documents have varied formats: some have inline citations, others have bibliographies, some embed methodology in footnotes. How do you handle this in few-shot examples?

options.text: Create a separate extraction prompt for each document format
Include few-shot examples demonstrating correct extraction from each format variation, showing Claude how to locate data in each structure
Preprocess all documents to a standard format before extraction
Use a higher temperature for more flexible interpretation

questions.stem: A structured extraction validates that line items sum to the stated total. The validation fails. How do you determine if the issue is extraction error or source document error?

options.text: Always assume extraction error - fix the prompt
Include both calculated_total (sum of line_items) and stated_total (from the document) in the schema; if they differ, flag conflict_detected: true and include both values for human review
Retry until both values match
Use the stated_total - it's always more reliable than the calculated value

questions.stem: What is the optimal few-shot example count for a code review task?

options.text: 1 - more examples consume too many tokens
2-4 carefully chosen examples covering the most common ambiguous cases (e.g., an issue that IS a bug, one that looks like a bug but isn't, one security issue, one acceptable pattern)
20+ examples for maximum coverage
No examples - explicit criteria are sufficient

questions.stem: You are designing a batch invoice processing pipeline. Invoices range from 1-50 pages. Some exceed the context limit. How do you handle the Batch API's lack of multi-turn tool calling?

options.text: Exclude long invoices - batch only supports short documents
Pre-process to chunk large invoices; submit each chunk as a separate batch item with custom_id reflecting the source document and chunk number; merge results post-processing
Use the synchronous API for long invoices and batch for short ones
Compress invoices to fit in the context limit before batching

questions.stem: Your code review system currently reports 45% false positives for 'style issues'. Developers are ignoring all reviews. What is the prioritized fix sequence?

options.text: Switch to a more accurate model immediately

(1) Temporarily disable the style category entirely to restore developer trust. (2) Analyze dismissed findings to identify specific false positive patterns. (3) Rewrite style criteria with explicit 'do not report' examples. (4) Re-enable with refined criteria.
Add 'only report critical style issues' to the prompt
Increase temperature to produce more varied findings

questions.stem: You need to extract financial data from documents written in English, Spanish, and German, each with different number formatting (1,000.00 vs 1.000,00). How does the prompt handle this?

options.text: Create separate prompts for each language
Include format normalization rules in the prompt: 'All monetary amounts must be converted to decimal notation (1234.56) regardless of source formatting' plus examples showing each format's conversion
Use a translation step before extraction
Use locale: auto in the JSON schema

questions.stem: When building a validation loop, how many retries are typically appropriate before escalating to human review?

options.text: Always retry until success
1-2 retries; beyond that, the error is likely unfixable with the same approach (absent information, fundamental format issue) - escalate to human review
5-10 retries to maximize automatic resolution
No retries - escalate immediately on first failure

questions.stem: You are building a batch pipeline and want to refine the prompt before processing 10,000 documents. What is the optimal approach?

options.text: Process all 10,000 and fix errors in post-processing
Run prompt refinement on a representative sample set (50-100 documents) covering format and content variations; validate precision and recall; only then batch-process the full set
Run on 100 documents, fix errors, run 900 more, fix errors - iterate until all 10,000 are done
Use the synchronous API for the first 1,000 before switching to batch

questions.stem: A PR review tool reports 60 issues. Developers say most are false positives. You want to identify which categories are causing the problem. What schema field helps most?

options.text: A severity field (critical/high/medium/low)
A detected_pattern field that captures which specific code construct triggered the finding, enabling analysis of which patterns are being over-flagged
A confidence field (0-1) that developers can filter on
A category field (bug/security/style)

questions.stem: How should you structure few-shot examples for a task that requires distinguishing between acceptable code patterns (project convention) and genuine bugs?

options.text: Only include examples of bugs - show Claude what's wrong

Include paired examples: one that LOOKS like a bug but IS an acceptable project convention (with reasoning), and one that IS a genuine bug (with reasoning). This teaches discrimination between the two.
Include only acceptable patterns so Claude knows what not to flag
Use generic examples not specific to your codebase

questions.stem: What is the correct approach for calculating the optimal batch submission frequency given: document SLA = 48 hours, batch processing max = 24 hours?

options.text: Submit every 48 hours
Submit every 24 hours - worst case: submitted at start of window, processed in 24 hours = delivered within 48-hour SLA with buffer
Submit every 12 hours for a 12-hour safety buffer
Use real-time API instead - batch doesn't meet the SLA

questions.stem: You have a code review prompt where false positives occur specifically when Claude encounters 'async/await in a loop'. How do you fix this?

options.text: Remove async/await detection from the prompt entirely

Add an explicit 'do not flag' rule with a concrete example: 'Sequential async/await in a loop is acceptable when operations must be ordered - example: [code example]. Only flag when the loop can be parallelized and the delay matters.'
Add 'ignore performance issues' to the prompt
Increase Claude's context window so it understands the full loop context

questions.stem: A batch job runs nightly with 1,000 documents. Some nights 50 documents fail with 'context length exceeded'. What is the efficient handling strategy?

options.text: Increase max_tokens and resubmit all 1,000 documents
Identify failed items by custom_id; chunk those specific documents and resubmit only the chunks as new batch items; merge the chunked results in post-processing
Skip oversized documents - they are too complex for batch processing
Switch to synchronous API for all documents when any fail

questions.stem: What is the 'Best of N' pattern in prompt engineering for structured output?

options.text: Generating N responses and taking the first valid one
Generating N independent responses to the same prompt and selecting the best using a scoring function - trading cost (N API calls) for quality (best result wins)
Running the prompt N times and taking the majority vote
Splitting a prompt into N sections and running each separately

questions.stem: How should you handle a JSON schema field that could validly be any of three types: a date string, a boolean, or a number?

options.text: Use anyOf: [{type: 'string'}, {type: 'boolean'}, {type: 'number'}]
Use type: 'string' and document that Claude should serialize the value as a string regardless of semantic type - then parse the string in your application code
Create separate schemas for each document type
Use type: 'object' with a value field

questions.stem: You need to validate that an extracted address is a real location without making API calls. What prompt engineering technique provides the best validation?

options.text: Ask Claude to validate the address after extraction in a separate call
Include a plausibility_score field in the schema (0-1) and an extraction_confidence field; include a few-shot example showing what a suspicious vs. normal address extraction looks like
Use regex to validate address format after extraction
Require extraction confidence > 0.9 before accepting

questions.stem: Your batch pipeline processes insurance claims. Some claims have no payout amount because they were denied. Your current schema requires payout_amount. How should you fix the schema?

options.text: Set payout_amount minimum to 0 to allow zero values
Make payout_amount nullable (type: ['number', 'null']) and add a claim_status field (enum: ['approved', 'denied', 'pending']) - null payout is valid for denied claims
Remove payout_amount from required fields but keep it non-nullable
Use a separate schema for denied claims

questions.stem: What is prompt chaining and when does it outperform a single complex prompt?

options.text: Linking multiple Claude sessions together
Breaking complex tasks into sequential steps where each step's output feeds the next - outperforms single prompts when the task has distinct phases that benefit from focused attention at each step
Using multiple models in a pipeline
Caching a sequence of prompts for reuse

questions.stem: You are refining a code review prompt and notice false positives specifically when Claude sees 'for..of loops with await inside'. How do you add the fix?

options.text: Add 'ignore all for loops' to the prompt

Add an explicit negative example to few-shot: 'This code: [for..of with await example] is ACCEPTABLE when operations must be sequential. Only flag if execution could be parallelized and performance matters.'
Remove performance review from the prompt scope
Add 'await in loops is acceptable' as a general rule

questions.stem: How should you design a system that uses the Batch API for primary processing but needs to handle urgent requests that arrive mid-batch?

options.text: Cancel the current batch and restart with the urgent request included
Maintain a dual-track system: synchronous API for urgent requests (real-time), batch API for standard requests (cost-optimized). Route based on urgency flag at submission time.
Process all requests in batch - urgency can wait for the next batch window
Use streaming for urgent requests within the batch API

questions.stem: You are building a prompt for a customer sentiment classification system. The current prompt produces 25% 'neutral' classifications for what developers believe are clearly positive or negative. What is the most likely issue?

options.text: The model needs more training data on neutral sentiment

The 'neutral' category boundaries are undefined - add explicit criteria: 'Classify as neutral ONLY when the customer expresses no evaluative language. If any positive or negative modifier exists, classify accordingly, even if mixed.'
Reduce the temperature to force more decisive classifications
Switch to a 5-category scale to capture more nuance

questions.stem: A document extraction system must handle tables with varying structures. Some tables have headers, some don't. Some have merged cells, some have hierarchical headers. How do you handle this in few-shot examples?

options.text: Include only well-formatted table examples - complex tables are edge cases
Include examples of each table variant: header/no-header, merged cells, hierarchical headers - each example shows the input table format and the correct extraction output
Pre-process all tables to a standard format before extraction
Add 'handle all table formats' to the system prompt

questions.stem: You want to add a 'self-review' step to your extraction pipeline where Claude checks its own output for consistency before returning it. What is the most effective implementation?

options.text: Ask Claude to 'review your output' in the same API call

Include consistency check fields in the extraction schema: {extracted_data: {...}, consistency_checks: {total_matches_line_items: bool, dates_in_valid_range: bool, required_fields_present: bool}, confidence: number}
Make a second API call asking Claude to validate the first call's output
Use extended thinking mode which automatically self-reviews

questions.stem: Your code review system needs to evaluate 'is this a security vulnerability?' for each finding. What few-shot example design produces the most reliable security classification?

options.text: Include 20+ diverse security examples to maximize coverage

Include paired examples: one code pattern that IS a security vulnerability (with explanation of the attack vector), and one similar-looking pattern that is NOT (with explanation of why it's safe). 3-4 pairs covering the most commonly confused categories.
Include only confirmed vulnerabilities - false examples confuse the model
Use a binary severity (vuln/not-vuln) without examples

questions.stem: You are designing a batch pipeline that extracts data from PDFs in multiple languages. Extraction quality is inconsistent for Japanese documents. What improvement strategy is most effective?

options.text: Add a translation step to convert Japanese to English before extraction

Add Japanese-language few-shot examples to the extraction prompt showing correct field extraction from Japanese invoice formats, including how Japanese date and number formats map to the output schema
Use a lower temperature for Japanese documents
Flag Japanese documents for manual review only

questions.stem: How should you structure a code review prompt to ensure coverage of both security and performance issues without trading one off for the other?

options.text: Use a single unified prompt that covers all review types

Define separate explicit criteria sections for each review dimension: SECURITY: [specific security criteria], PERFORMANCE: [specific performance criteria]. Each finding must be tagged with its dimension. Results show both dimensions independently.
Run security review first, then performance in a separate call
Ask Claude to 'balance security and performance considerations'

questions.stem: You are designing a prompt for extracting medical dosage information from clinical notes. Dosages appear in many formats: '10mg', '10 milligrams', 'ten mg', '0.01g'. How do you handle normalization most reliably?

options.text: Let Claude normalize whatever format it encounters - it understands units

Provide explicit normalization rules: 'Convert all dosages to milligrams (numeric only). Conversion: 1g = 1000mg. Write out numbers: ten = 10. Return: {drug: string, dose_mg: number}' plus examples for each format variant.
Extract raw text and normalize with a post-processing library
Use separate extraction prompts for each format variant

questions.stem: How do you prompt Claude to produce a structured output that includes both extracted data AND a confidence assessment for the entire extraction?

options.text: Make a second API call asking Claude to rate its previous extraction

Include confidence fields in the initial extraction schema: {extracted_data: {...}, extraction_confidence: 0-1, low_confidence_fields: ['field1', 'field2'], extraction_notes: 'string for unusual situations'}
Use extended thinking mode - it provides confidence automatically
Confidence assessment is not possible in single-call extractions

questions.stem: You are building an invoice extraction system and notice that Claude extracts correct values on 95% of invoices but fails on those with non-standard layouts (tabular data in headers, multi-column line items). How do you address this?

options.text: Accept 95% accuracy - non-standard invoices are rare

Add few-shot examples specifically for non-standard layouts; include a layout_detection field in the schema (standard/tabular-header/multi-column) that Claude fills in before extraction; use the detected layout to route to the appropriate extraction approach
Pre-process all invoices to a standard layout before extraction
Use a different model for non-standard layouts

questions.stem: How do you design a prompt for summarization that produces consistent length across inputs of varying length (100-word memos to 50-page reports)?

options.text: Set a fixed max_tokens - length will naturally vary with input

Specify proportional length: 'Produce a summary of approximately 10% of the original length, with a minimum of 50 words and maximum of 500 words. For very short inputs (< 100 words), a 2-3 sentence summary is sufficient.'
Summarize all inputs to exactly 100 words
Let Claude determine the appropriate length based on content density

questions.stem: You are designing a high-accuracy medical document extraction system. What combination of techniques maximizes reliability?

options.text: Use claude-opus with high temperature for creative interpretation
Tool use with nullable fields + retry-with-feedback loop (max 2) + confidence scoring schema + human review queue for low-confidence extractions + few-shot examples for medical terminology variants
Multiple models in ensemble with majority voting
Strict required fields (no nullables) to force complete extraction

questions.stem: You need to extract data from 50,000 legal contracts with three extraction schemas (depending on contract type: NDA, SLA, Purchase Agreement). What is the optimal prompt engineering architecture?

options.text: One universal schema for all contract types

Contract type classifier fi route to type-specific extraction schema. Each schema uses tool_choice forced selection + type-specific few-shot examples + type-specific validation logic. Batch process by contract type for prompt cache efficiency.
Three separate batch jobs running simultaneously
One schema with all possible fields, most nullable

questions.stem: A production extraction system has 2% unexplained failures where validation fails for no apparent reason. Debugging reveals the issue occurs only with documents that contain tables with merged cells. How do you address this?

options.text: Add 'handle tables with merged cells' to the prompt

Add a targeted few-shot example showing correct extraction from a merged-cell table, with a note in the system prompt: 'For tables with merged cells, treat the merged cell value as applying to all spanned rows/columns'
Pre-process documents to convert merged cells to repeated values before extraction
Flag all documents with tables for human review

questions.stem: You are building a prompt optimization feedback loop. Developer dismissals of review findings are logged with the finding context. After 3 months, you have 50,000 dismissal records. How do you use this data most effectively?

options.text: Delete all findings that were dismissed more than once
Cluster dismissals by detected_pattern; identify top-10 false positive patterns by frequency; create targeted 'do not report' examples for each; A/B test prompt variants before deploying
Use the data to fine-tune a custom Claude model
Lower confidence threshold for all findings

questions.stem: You are designing a structured extraction system for financial filings that must achieve 99.9% accuracy on the primary fields. What quality assurance architecture achieves this?

options.text: A single extraction call with high-quality few-shot examples

Multi-stage: (1) extraction with confidence scoring, (2) independent cross-validation extraction, (3) comparison for conflicts, (4) human review queue for conflicts or low-confidence, (5) ongoing false-positive/negative tracking
Run the same extraction 10 times and take the majority vote
Use claude-opus exclusively - it has 99.9% accuracy

questions.stem: How do you design a system where the Batch API handles primary processing but some batch failures should be retried synchronously with richer context?

options.text: All failures should use the same retry strategy

After batch processing: categorize failures by error type. For transient errors (context limits, timeouts): synchronous retry with document chunking and richer prompt context. For semantic validation failures: synchronous retry with specific error feedback. For missing-data failures: route to human review (retrying won't help).
Re-submit all failures to a new batch
Log failures and process them in the next day's batch

questions.stem: You need to build a self-improving extraction system. When human reviewers correct extraction errors, how should these corrections be incorporated?

options.text: Manually rewrite the prompt after each correction

Store corrections with original input + error + correction as structured examples; periodically analyze patterns; add high-frequency patterns as few-shot negative examples; validate improvement before deploying prompt updates
Fine-tune a custom Claude model on correction data
Use the corrections as batch API training data

questions.stem: A complex extraction task requires understanding document structure, entity resolution, cross-reference validation, and output generation. Single-prompt performance is inconsistent. What architecture solves this?

options.text: Use extended thinking mode for better reasoning

Decompose into a prompt chain: (1) document structure analysis, (2) entity extraction with structure context, (3) cross-reference validation with entities, (4) output generation with validated entities. Each stage receives focused input from the prior stage.
Increase temperature for more creative interpretation
Use a single larger prompt with all context simultaneously

questions.stem: You are building a code review system where the same PR should receive different review criteria based on which team owns the changed files (payment team fi PCI compliance, auth team fi security hardening, data team fi privacy). How do you implement this?

options.text: One universal review prompt for all file changes

Detect file ownership from CODEOWNERS; select team-specific review criteria; inject appropriate few-shot examples for that team's standards; force the extraction schema fields relevant to that team's compliance requirements
Create separate CI jobs per team
Let the reviewer decide which criteria to apply based on the PR description

questions.stem: Your extraction pipeline processes documents in real-time for a user-facing feature and in batch overnight for analytics. The same extraction logic must be used in both modes. How do you architect this?

options.text: Duplicate the extraction logic - real-time and batch have different requirements

Abstract the extraction function to be mode-agnostic (same prompt, same schema, same validation); build a thin routing layer that wraps it in synchronous API calls for real-time and Batch API submission for overnight runs
Use different models for real-time (haiku for speed) vs. batch (opus for quality)
The Batch API format is incompatible with synchronous extraction - they must be separate

questions.stem: When designing a prompt for extracting information from handwritten forms (OCR'd to text), what additional few-shot techniques improve accuracy?

options.text: The same techniques as for printed documents - OCR doesn't change the approach

Add few-shot examples specifically showing OCR artifacts (misspellings, character substitutions, run-together words) and how to correctly interpret them; add a transcription_notes field for ambiguous characters
Pre-process OCR text with a spell-checker before extraction
Use a lower confidence threshold for handwritten forms

questions.stem: You need to batch-process 10,000 invoices. After testing, 500 invoices reliably exceed the context limit. What is the cost-optimal resubmission strategy?

options.text: Use the synchronous API for all 10,000 to handle the 500 edge cases
Submit 9,500 normal invoices to batch (50% savings). For the 500 large invoices: chunk each into sections, create chunk-level batch items (still 50% savings), post-process to merge chunk results.
Skip the 500 oversized invoices
Use a larger model with bigger context for all 10,000

questions.stem: A prompt produces correct output 95% of the time but fails unpredictably on the remaining 5%. You've collected 50 failure examples. What is the systematic improvement process?

options.text: Add 'be more careful' to the system prompt
Cluster the 50 failures by root cause; identify the top 3 failure patterns; create targeted few-shot negative examples for each; A/B test the improved prompt against the original before deploying
Switch to a more capable model to reduce the failure rate
Increase max_tokens to give Claude more room to think

questions.stem: What is the most reliable way to ensure that required fields in a JSON extraction schema are only marked as required when you are certain the source documents always contain them?

options.text: Mark all fields as required - missing data indicates extraction failure
Analyze a representative sample of source documents before finalizing the schema; only mark a field as required if it appears in 99%+ of sampled documents; make all other fields nullable
Start with all fields required and remove from required when extraction fails
Never use required - make all fields optional

questions.stem: You are building a knowledge extraction pipeline for a legal firm. Contracts contain complex clause structures: main clauses, sub-clauses, and exceptions to sub-clauses. Standard extraction produces incorrect nesting 30% of the time. How do you solve this systematically?

options.text: Extract all clauses as a flat list and post-process the hierarchy

Multi-stage extraction: Stage 1 maps document structure (identifies clause IDs and hierarchy), Stage 2 extracts clause content using IDs as anchors, Stage 3 validates hierarchy consistency. Include hierarchical schema {clause_id, parent_clause_id, clause_type, content, exceptions: []}.
Use regex to detect clause markers and build the hierarchy
Provide 20 few-shot examples covering all hierarchy patterns

questions.stem: How do you design a prompt engineering strategy for a task where ground truth is difficult to establish (e.g., 'tone analysis' of marketing copy)?

options.text: Skip tone analysis - subjective tasks are not suitable for Claude

Operationalize the subjective concept: define specific tone dimensions (formality, energy, warmth) as measurable scales (1-5) with explicit anchors for each level. Include 3-4 calibration examples per dimension where domain experts agree on scores. Test inter-rater reliability between Claude and human experts.
Use confidence scores to flag uncertain tone assessments
Accept that tone analysis will be inconsistent - this is inherent to subjective tasks

questions.stem: You are building a medical coding system that maps clinical text to ICD-10 codes. Accuracy is critical. What prompt engineering and validation architecture maximizes accuracy?

options.text: Few-shot examples with 10 ICD-10 code examples

Multi-component accuracy architecture: (1) primary extraction with structured schema {code, description, confidence, supporting_text}, (2) independent validation extraction on same input, (3) comparison for disagreements, (4) disagreement routing to specialist review, (5) ongoing calibration against confirmed diagnoses from EHR system
Use the largest Claude model - capability determines accuracy
Post-validate codes against the ICD-10 database for validity

questions.stem: You are designing a prompt that must work reliably for inputs in 30 languages including right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and ideographic scripts (Japanese, Chinese). What prompt engineering considerations apply?

options.text: Translate all inputs to English before processing

Test extraction quality per language family; define how to handle mixed-language inputs (transliteration, code-switching); specify script-aware normalization rules (Chinese traditional vs simplified); include examples from each script family; specify that output JSON field names are always in English regardless of content language
Use separate Claude instances for different language families
Claude handles all languages equally - no special considerations needed

questions.stem: How do you build a self-improving prompt pipeline where the prompt automatically evolves based on extraction errors?

options.text: Prompt improvement requires manual human effort - automation is not possible

Automated refinement loop: extraction fi validation fi error classification fi error pattern analysis (cluster similar errors) fi generate targeted prompt patches for top error patterns fi A/B test patches fi deploy winning patch fi repeat. Track error rate over time as the improvement metric.
Use Claude to generate new prompts from scratch each week
Fine-tune a custom model on extraction errors

questions.stem: A legal contract extraction system must extract obligations (what each party must do) with temporal references (when obligations trigger or expire). Temporal references are complex ('within 30 days of material breach, unless previously waived'). How do you design the extraction schema and prompts?

options.text: Extract obligations and temporal references as plain text strings

Structured temporal schema: {obligation_text, party, trigger_event, trigger_timing: {type: 'relative/absolute/conditional', value: string, reference_point: string}, expiry: {type, value}, conditions: [string], obligation_type: 'must/may/must_not'}. Include few-shot examples for each trigger_timing type.
Extract only absolute dates - relative temporal references are too complex
Use a separate NLP library for temporal expression parsing

questions.stem: You are designing a content moderation system that must handle cultural nuance content acceptable in one cultural context may be inappropriate in another. How do you implement culturally-aware classification?

options.text: Apply universal content standards - cultural variation cannot be systematically handled

Culture-aware classification: include target_market field in input; maintain culture-specific few-shot example sets; classification schema includes {decision, primary_culture_context, cross_cultural_considerations, confidence}. Build a culture-expert review pipeline for uncertain cross-cultural cases.
Default to the most restrictive standard across all cultures
Use a separate model per cultural region

questions.stem: How do you implement 'extraction conflict resolution' when multiple sources in a document provide contradictory values for the same field?

options.text: Take the first occurrence - consistency over recency

Extract all occurrences with source location: {value, location, context}. Apply resolution rules documented in the prompt (e.g., 'for price: use the summary table value if present, otherwise the line item total'). Include conflict_detected: true when resolution is ambiguous and both values for human review.
Take the most recent occurrence - documents build on earlier content
Flag the document as invalid and reject it

questions.stem: You need to extract information from handwritten forms that have been OCR-processed. OCR errors are common (l/1, O/0, rn/m, missing spaces). How do you design prompts that are resilient to OCR noise?

options.text: Fix OCR quality before extraction - garbage in, garbage out

OCR-resilient extraction: document OCR error patterns in the prompt; instruct Claude to interpret likely-OCR-corrupted text using context clues; include OCR noise examples in few-shot data; schema includes extraction_confidence and ocr_correction_applied fields for audit
Use strict pattern matching - reject extractions with likely OCR errors
OCR correction is the preprocessing tool's problem - extraction assumes clean text

questions.stem: How do you design a Batch API workflow that handles documents arriving continuously throughout the day with varying urgency levels?

options.text: Accumulate all documents and submit one batch per day

Multi-tier submission strategy: urgent documents fi synchronous API (immediate). Standard documents fi collected into hourly micro-batches for 50% cost reduction with 1-hour maximum latency. End-of-day cleanup batch for any remaining items. Route based on urgency tag at document ingestion.
Use the Batch API for everything with urgency handled by polling frequency
Submit individual batch requests for each document as it arrives

questions.stem: You are building a system that extracts financial metrics from earnings call transcripts. Some metrics are stated directly ('revenue grew 12%') and others require calculation from stated numbers ('gross margin = (revenue - COGS) / revenue'). How do you design extraction + calculation in a single pass?

options.text: Extract stated metrics only - calculations introduce error risk

Schema with derivation tracking: {metric_name, stated_value (if directly stated), calculated_value (if derived), calculation_formula (if derived), source_values: [values used in calculation], derivation_confidence}. Instruct Claude to show work for calculated metrics.
Two separate passes: one for extraction, one for calculation
Pre-calculate all derived metrics before extraction to simplify the task

questions.stem: How do you ensure that your Batch API pipeline for document processing maintains FIFO ordering for documents that must be processed in sequence?

options.text: Batch API guarantees FIFO processing - no special handling needed

Sequence enforcement outside the Batch API: assign sequence_number to documents, track dependencies in a coordinator, only submit document N+1 to batch after document N's result is confirmed. For independent documents, batch freely. Batch API makes no ordering guarantees.
Use batch priority flags to enforce ordering
Process sequential documents synchronously and batch the rest

questions.stem: A document extraction system must handle both dense technical documents (50,000 tokens) and short forms (500 tokens) using the same extraction prompt and schema. How do you optimize for both?

options.text: Use different models for short and long documents

Adaptive chunking strategy: for documents under 4,000 tokens, single-pass extraction. For longer documents, hierarchical extraction: first pass creates a structured outline with section summaries, second pass extracts detailed fields from relevant sections identified in the outline.
Use the full 200K context window for all documents - no special handling needed
Truncate all documents to 4,000 tokens for consistency

questions.stem: You need to design a prompt for extracting relationships between entities in text (e.g., 'Company A acquired Company B for $X'). Relationships can span multiple sentences. How do you handle cross-sentence relationship extraction?

options.text: Extract only within-sentence relationships - cross-sentence is too complex

Multi-sentence relationship schema: {relationship_type, subject_entity, object_entity, relationship_attributes (amount, date, etc.), evidence_sentences: [sentence indices where evidence appears], confidence, requires_inference: boolean}. Few-shot examples showing relationships requiring evidence across 2-3 sentences.
Pre-process text into single-sentence units before extraction
Use a dependency parser to identify relationships, then Claude for details

questions.stem: How do you evaluate prompt quality for a structured extraction task at scale when manual evaluation of 10,000 results is infeasible?

options.text: Sample 100 results randomly and extrapolate quality

Automated evaluation pipeline: (1) syntactic validation (schema compliance, 100% automatable), (2) semantic validation (value consistency rules, ~70% automatable), (3) reference dataset comparison for key metrics (precision/recall on labeled subset), (4) drift detection (monitor metric distributions over time for unexpected shifts)
Use a second Claude call to evaluate each extraction
Only evaluate on cases where downstream processing fails

questions.stem: How do you design a prompt that handles 'nested optional structures' in extraction where a document may have 0, 1, or many instances of a section, each with its own sub-structure?

options.text: Extract each section type in a separate API call

Array-based schema with nullable sections: {mandatory_fields: {...}, optional_section_a: [{field1, field2, ...}] | null, optional_section_b: [{...}] | null}. Instruct Claude: 'If section X is absent, set it to null. If present, extract all instances as array elements.' Include examples for 0, 1, and 2+ instances.
Force all documents to have all sections by filling absent ones with defaults
Use a two-pass approach: first detect which sections exist, then extract each

findings.detail: Difficulty distribution is heavily skewed towards levels 2 and 3, with no questions at the highest (5) or lowest (1) levels. This is acceptable given the small sample size and single domain.
